_note: 2024 PHB feats — Origin (level 1, background/Human) and Fighting Style (require the Fighting Style feature). Benefit text is original paraphrase of mechanics; source 'phb'.

feats.name: Alert
benefits: Initiative Proficiency: You add your Proficiency Bonus to Initiative rolls.
Initiative Swap: Immediately after rolling Initiative you can swap your Initiative with a willing ally in the same combat (you can't do this if either of you is Incapacitated).

feats.name: Crafter
benefits: Tool Proficiency: You gain proficiency with three types of Artisan's Tools of your choice.
Discount: Whenever you buy a nonmagical item you get a 20% discount.
Fast Crafting: When you finish a Long Rest you can craft one piece of gear from a set list (using tools you're proficient with) faster than normal.

feats.name: Healer
benefits: Battle Medic: As a Utilize action you can expend one use of a Healer's Kit to let a creature within 5 feet regain Hit Points equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus, plus their number of Hit Dice; a creature can't benefit again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.
Healing Reroll: Whenever you roll a die to restore Hit Points with a spell or feature, you can reroll a 1 and must use the new roll.

feats.name: Lucky
benefits: Luck Points: You have a number of Luck Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regained on a Long Rest.
Advantage: When you roll a d20 for a D20 Test you can spend 1 Luck Point to give yourself Advantage on the roll.
Disadvantage: When a creature rolls a d20 to attack you, you can spend 1 Luck Point to give that roll Disadvantage.

feats.name: Magic Initiate
benefits: Two Cantrips: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list (choose one list; that list's ability is your spellcasting ability for these spells).
Level 1 Spell: Choose one level 1 spell from that same list; you always have it prepared and can cast it once without a spell slot per Long Rest (or using slots you have).
Swap: Whenever you gain a level you can replace one of these spells with another from the same list.

feats.name: Musician
benefits: Instrument Proficiency: You gain proficiency with three Musical Instruments of your choice.
Encouraging Song: When you finish a Short or Long Rest you can play a tune and give Heroic Inspiration to allies who hear it, up to a number equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

feats.name: Savage Attacker
benefits: Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon's damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.

feats.name: Skilled
benefits: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

feats.name: Tavern Brawler
benefits: Ability Score: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1 (max 20).
Enhanced Unarmed Strike: Your Unarmed Strike deals 1d4 damage instead of 1.
Damage Rerolls: Whenever you roll damage for your Unarmed Strike, you can reroll a 1 and must use the new roll.

Improvised Proficiency & Push: You're proficient with improvised weapons, and once per turn when you hit with an Unarmed Strike you can deal extra damage or push the target 5 feet as part of the hit (a Bonus Action grapple/shove option).

feats.name: Tough
benefits: Your Hit Point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you take this feat, and by 2 each time you gain a level thereafter.

feats.name: Archery
benefits: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with Ranged weapons.

feats.name: Blind Fighting
benefits: You have Blindsight with a range of 10 feet, letting you see anything within that range that isn't behind Total Cover, even if you're Blinded or in Darkness.

feats.name: Defense
benefits: While you're wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

feats.name: Dueling
benefits: When you're wielding a Melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

feats.name: Great Weapon Fighting
benefits: When you roll damage for a Melee weapon you're wielding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property.

feats.name: Interception
benefits: When a creature you can see hits another creature within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use a Reaction to reduce that damage by 1d10 + your Proficiency Bonus (minimum 0). You must be wielding a weapon or Shield.

feats.name: Protection
benefits: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you within 5 feet of you, you can use a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a Shield.

feats.name: Thrown Weapon Fighting
benefits: You can draw a weapon that has the Thrown property as part of the attack you make with it, and you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with such thrown weapon attacks.

feats.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
benefits: When you make an extra attack with a different Light weapon as a Bonus Action, you can add your ability modifier to that attack's damage.

feats.name: Unarmed Fighting
benefits: Your Unarmed Strikes deal 1d6 bludgeoning on a hit (1d8 if you have no weapon or Shield in either hand). If you have a creature Grappled, at the start of each of your turns you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to it.

feats.name: Druidic Warrior
benefits: You learn two Druid cantrips of your choice, cast using Wisdom. Whenever you gain a level you can swap one of them for another Druid cantrip.
